highlights: The first NFL Sunday of the season is here. The player prop market is full of different ways to get in on the action. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season.

He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals.

They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players.

results.title: 2026 NFL Week 2 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Back Commanders To Cover At Cowboys
results.description: Geoff Schwartz is back with his NFL Week 2 wagers, including his bet on the NFC East showdown between the Commanders and Cowboys.
highlights: The Commanders almost got the win against the Eagles in Week 1, but now they get another chance to prove their worth in the NFC East against Dallas. Find out why I'm backing Washington to cover against its division rival and check out how I'm wagering on Bengals-Texans. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports This is a huge NFC East division game and both teams are scrambling for a win after they both dropped their Week 1 tilts. I like the Commanders to keep this game close. Washington lost by two points to the Eagles last weekend and could have won the game. The Eagles only generated 10 first downs but hit multiple explosive plays to score. The Commanders' offense played well (at times) against one of the better defenses in the NFL. Now it faces a Dallas defense that was pathetic on Sunday night against the Giants. The Cowboys' defensive line got dominated by the Giants and the coverage unit got beat multiple times with the same concept.

There was a lot of chatter after Week 1 that the Bengals' defense was fixed and that's all because they beat the Bucs 33-27. The Bucs scored late to make it a one-score game. It was a Bengals double-digit lead for most of the day. However, if you take a closer look, it’s easy to see that the Bengals' defense did not play as well as reported. The Bucs fumbled the ball four times and the Bengals do get credit for forcing those turnovers. But the Bucs scored on every other drive. They had no punts and 50% on third down. CJ Stroud and the Texans had a solid showing against the Bills in Week 1 (Getty Images). The Texans' offense played well against the Bills on Sunday. It scored 31 points and more importantly, the run game was much improved. Houston spent resources on the offensive line and at running back. It looked much better than it did in 2025. Also, the pass protection looked better.

CJ Stroud looked comfortable and more confident. I’d also look for the Texans to be aggressive in this game since they need a win. They cannot start 0-2 against two teams contending for the AFC. So I’d expect them to score points. Schwartz's Pick: Texans Over 23.5 points scored Get more from the National Football League Follow your favorites to get information about games, news and more

Jahmyr Gibbs Over 90.5 Rushing Yards (-110) There is plenty of talent across this Lions’ offense, but it has become increasingly evident that Jahmyr Gibbs is the foundation of the attack. After splitting carries with David Montgomery to start his career, Detroit now leans on the Alabama product as their bell-cow back. Gibbs tallied a career-high and NFL-leading 29 carries in Week 1, turning these opportunities into 156 yards and two touchdowns. Buffalo holds plenty of defensive concerns of their own entering this matchup.

Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Thursday Night Football Week 2 of NFL action kicks off with a thrilling Thursday Night Football battle between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Bills. Both teams have deep playoff aspirations and picked up Week 1 victories. The Bills fended off the Texans 36-31, while the Lions were pushed to the limit in a 31-30 overtime victory against the Saints. They will now square off in a measuring stick matchup against each other to kick off the second week of the season. Looking at the odds, the Bills enter as 5.5-point favorites with -230 Moneyline odds on DraftKings Sportsbook. The Lions hold +190 odds to pull off the upset, with the game total set at 54.5 points. Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets for Thursday Night Football

This is a Texans’ defense that finished last season ranked second in opponents’ points allowed, first in yards conceded, and sixth in opponents’ passing yards last season. They were widely expected to have a case for one of the top defensive units in football this year, but will need to make some major improvements from their Week 1 performance if this is to be the case. But the impressive output should say more about Allen than the Texans’ defense. The Bills’ star had a bit of a down season last year in his passing metrics, averaging 215.8 passing yards per game. But he is averaging 235.9 passing yards per game in his career and tallied as many as 284.0 over a season. Allen still tallied 253 passing yards or greater in seven games ,even with it being a down year in passing production last year. Allen will also be able to feast on this Lions’ defense, given the concerns mentioned above. Tyler Shough aired the ball out for 410 passing yards and three touchdowns against them last week to provide the upset scare.
